model_rationale: It prints debug lines 'v->>%d' before the answer, so every test fails on output (0/11). No loop-boundary error.
For i == n-1 it prints the last id twice ('%d\n' and then '%d '), an output-format bug; the loop bounds are right.
The print loop runs i < y and then prints sap[y-1] again, so the last id appears twice. Changing the bound to y-1 makes every test pass (repair-verified); this is count arithmetic.
x[1000] (float) holds n ratios while d/multa are sized 100000, so for n > 1000 x overflows (ASan global-buffer-overflow). Undersized fixed array.
The output format and loop bounds are right (6/11 pass); the tie-break compares d instead of keeping input order, a comparator logic error.
The print loop skips the last element ('if (i != n-1)' prints nothing for it), so only n-1 ids are output, a count off by one. The comparator also has no tie-break, which may break other tests.
div[] is never computed: the local array is compared and swapped while still uninitialised, so the order is garbage.
'final = sap[i][n-1]' uses n-1 as the second index of a [n][2] array, far past index 1 for n > 2 (ASan dynamic-stack overflow).
Each row is malloc'd with 2 floats but indices [2] and [3] are written, two past the end (ASan heap-buffer-overflow). This is an undersized allocation, not an off-by-one.
g[MAX=100] holds L edges (L can exceed 100), and func() also reads g[L] with 'i <= L'. ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow, but 1/11 also points to a wrong component-count algorithm.
'while (i < n)' skips node n when counting components; changing '<' to '<=' makes every oracle test pass (repair-verified).
Prints a debug line '%d = %d' for every component, so every test fails on output (0/11). MAX = 100 also overflows on the large test, but that is secondary.
adj[100][100] / vis[100] for N up to 1000: it fails only the large test, with an ASan global-buffer-overflow. Undersized fixed array.
dfs() is never called, so every unvisited node counts as a component (2/11). Logic error; the array size only matters on the large test.
Prints 'dfs(i);' debug lines and starts at node 0, so every test with edges fails on output.
